title: Concordance Between [<sup>18</sup>F]Flortaucipir PET Visual Reads and CenTauR-Based Quantification.
abstract: Tau PET imaging with [18F]flortaucipir allows for the visualization and mapping of aggregated tau deposits, a key neuropathologic feature of Alzheimer disease (AD). A visual interpretation method for [18F]flortaucipir was approved by the Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency and has been implemented for a standardized, clinically usable definition of tau PET positivity. The CenTauRz method, on the other hand, offers the possibility to harmonize the definition of tau PET positivity across different radiotracers using quantitative metrics, but its concordance with clinically relevant [18F]flortaucipir visual reads remains unclear. Methods: A convenience sample of 3991 participants, including cognitively unimpaired (CU) and cognitively impaired (CI) individuals (i.e., those with mild cognitive impairment or AD dementia), underwent [18F]flortaucipir PET imaging. Each [18F]flortaucipir scan was assessed by 3 trained readers using the approved visual interpretation method and quantified using the CenTauRz quantification pipeline in different regions of interest (ROIs). Concordance between positive visual reads and CenTauRz-defined positivity (i.e., >2 on the CenTauRz scale) was assessed using Cohen κ. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the discriminative power of continuous CenTauRz values in distinguishing between negative and positive visual reads. Generalized additive models examined clinical progression on the basis of visual and CenTauRz-based assessments of tau PET positivity. Results: Concordance between visual reads and CenTauRz-based assessments of tau PET positivity was moderate, particularly in CU individuals (κ = 0.23-0.55 for CU participants, κ = 0.57-0.82 for CI participants, depending on the ROI). ROC analysis revealed that the agreement remained moderate, independent of the CenTauRz cut point used (area under the ROC curve, 0.72-0.87 vs. 0.87-0.97 for CU and CI individuals, respectively). Among discordant cases, participants with visually positive/CenTauRz-negative tau PET scans were more frequently amyloid-positive and exhibited faster clinical progression compared with visually negative/CenTauRz-positive individuals. Conclusion: Our findings highlight the relatively limited agreement between the visual assessment of [18F]flortaucipir PET images and CenTauRz-based quantification, particularly in CU individuals. Participants with visually positive/CenTauRz-negative tau PET scans showed a high frequency of amyloid positivity and faster clinical progression, suggesting that visual reads are more sensitive to heterogeneous, clinically relevant tau accumulation patterns not captured by ROI-based methods. These findings underscore the need for new quantification approaches to better capture the complex patterns of tau deposition, important for early AD detection and monitoring.

title: Navigating Complexity and Wicked Problems in Technology Integration with Design Thinking: AMEE Guide No. 193.
abstract: Technological change has become increasingly common in this era of digitalisation, with new technologies frequently introduced to enhance teaching and learning. However, as with any change, the implementation of technology is rarely straightforward. Unintended consequences, contextual constraints, and disruptions to existing practices can create significant challenges and barriers to successful digital transformation. Introducing a new technology often requires changes across multiple layers of complex educational systems. We therefore ask: What are the challenges and ways forward in respect of the planning, development and implementation of technological change in health professions education? In this AMEE Guide, we propose that technological change within the complexity of health professions education can be understood as a wicked problem. After considering this in depth, we then explore design thinking as an operational approach for navigating such complexity through iterative problem framing, stakeholder engagement, prototyping, testing, and refinement. We use the development lifecycle of a learning analytics dashboard as an example to examine the systemic challenges that arise when introducing digital transformation into health professions education. The Guide concludes by considering implications for future research and practice and presenting a set of Practice Points to support educators and institutions undertaking technological change.

title: Vector Matters: A Critical Review of Biomechanics, Safety, and Evidence Quality in Aesthetic Rib Remodeling.
abstract: Aesthetic rib remodeling includes parallel corticotomy, perpendicular puncture, and rib-resection approaches, but comparative safety remains uncertain. We conducted a structured narrative review of evidence published from January 2015 through June 2026. Clinical reports, systematic reviews, functional studies, directly relevant biomechanical work, and official publication-status notices were considered. Three reviewers screened the original evidence independently and resolved disagreements by consensus. Historical record-level exports and extraction sheets were not retained; therefore, no retrospective screening counts or pooled unique-patient total were reconstructed. The literature consists mainly of uncontrolled observational reports with heterogeneous selection, cointerventions, techniques, surveillance, follow-up, and potentially overlapping cohorts. Published parallel-technique cohorts appear less morbid in their reporting of major pleural events than some perpendicular-technique reports, but no head-to-head comparison, adjusted analysis, or verified unique pooled denominator establishes a causal safety advantage. Recent RibXcar reports include pulmonary-function, imaging, complication, fatalities, and patient-reported outcome data, although cohort overlap cannot be excluded. Ultrasound may assist localization, visualization, and documentation, but its incremental safety or efficacy effect has not been isolated. Current evidence supports cautious technique-specific reporting and prospective comparative studies with unique denominators, standardized complication surveillance, operator and technique-fidelity documentation, adequate follow-up, and validated patient-reported outcomes.

title: Real-time XR-based 6-DOF catheter tracking enhances cardiac intervention navigation efficiency and depth perception.
abstract: Despite advances in 3D ultrasound, most percutaneous cardiac interventions still rely on 2D visualization, limiting depth perception and spatial understanding. To address this challenge, we developed an Extended Reality (XR)-based platform that enables real-time six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) catheter tracking and visualization within a patient-specific 3D heart model. The system combines a custom machine-vision algorithm for 5-DOF catheter tracking with a 3D-printed electromechanical encoder that measures catheter roll, providing complete 6-DOF motion reconstruction. In a proof-of-concept study, 20 novice medical students navigated an intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) catheter to six anatomical targets using either immersive 3D visualization or a conventional 2D cathlab-style view. Participants in the 3D condition completed the task in 54.6 seconds and traveled 1939 mm on average, compared with 263.5 seconds and 7854 mm in the 2D condition. The ratio of cohort means was 4.8× for completion time and 4.1× for travel length (means of subject-level ratios: 5.1× and 4.9×). The 3D mode also produced more direct and less variable approach trajectories. Participants consistently rated immersive visualization higher for accuracy, speed, usability, and clinical value. Exploratory kinematic analysis suggested that 3D users distributed motion more evenly along the depth axis, whereas 2D users relied more on lateral and vertical adjustments. These findings demonstrate that XR-based visualization can substantially improve procedural training efficiency and motor control.

title: Small-molecule fluorescent probes for non-destructive DNA detection: a systematic review of molecular skeletons, design strategies, and biological applications.
abstract: DNA detection and imaging are essential for elucidating genomic regulation, diagnosing diseases, and developing therapeutic agents. Small-molecule fluorescent probes serve as powerful non-destructive tools that enable the structural detection and visualization of DNA without compromising cellular or nucleic acid integrity. Based on their molecular skeletons, this review systematically summarizes advances in this field over the past decade. Seven categories of fluorophores are discussed: carbazole, benzothiazole/thiazole orange, pyridinium/quinolinium, triphenylamine, BODIPY, pyrene/tribenzoarene, and cyanine/coumarin derivatives. This review focuses primarily on their photophysical properties, fluorescence response mechanisms, non-covalent binding modes, and structural selectivity, as well as rational design strategies for the specific recognition of G-quadruplex, double-stranded DNA, i-motif, and three-way junction structures. Finally, future perspectives on the development of next-generation DNA-targeted probes for live-cell imaging and clinical translation are discussed.

title: Combination Therapy of Injectables With Energy-Based Treatments for Facial Rejuvenation: An Updated Review.
abstract:
Background

Fillers are frequently combined with other injectables and energy-based devices to target volume loss, dynamic rhytides, and photodamage. Questions remain regarding optimal treatment sequencing, safety, and synergistic clinical efficacy.OBJECTIVETo evalute the current evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of combining injectable therapies with energy-based treatments for facial rejuvenation.

Methods

MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched using keywords on dermal fillers with neuromodulators, intense pulsed light (IPL), laser, microfocused ultrasound with visualization (MFU-V), high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), or radiofrequency (RF). Studies reporting safety, efficacy, sequencing, or clinical outcomes were included.

Results

Combining fillers with neuromodulators produces synergistic improvements in facial rejuvenation by addressing volume loss and muscular hyperactivity with superior outcomes and longer treatment durability compared with monotherapy. Intense pulsed light, nonablative lasers, MFU-V, HIFU, and RF appear safe when used with fillers, with studies demonstrating no significant adverse interactions or compromise of filler integrity. Combination treatment may enhance optimize facial contouring, improve skin quality, and improve patient satisfaction and retention. Histologic and clinical studies suggest synergistic effects when MFU-V/RF are combined with biostimulatory fillers.

Conclusion

Combination treatment with fillers and complementary modalities offers a comprehensive approach to facial rejuvenation. Current evidence supports the safety of most nonablative combination protocols. Additional studies are needed to assess the safety and efficacy of combining fillers with more aggressive resurfacing procedures and novel devices.

title: Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Trans-Kambin Lumbar Interbody Fusion at the L5/S1 Level: A Consecutive Case Series With 1-Year Clinical and Radiological Outcomes.
abstract:
Background

Trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1 is technically demanding because of reduced disc height, a narrow safety triangle, anatomical variability of the exiting nerve root (ENR), foraminal pathology, and interference from the iliac crest. This study evaluated the feasibility and 1-year clinical and radiological outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1 in a consecutive case series.

Methods

This retrospective consecutive case series included 25 patients who underwent single-level UBE trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1 between January 2023 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Oswestry Disability Index and numerical rating scale scores for low back pain and leg pain. Radiological outcomes included segmental lordotic angle, slip distance, and preliminary computed tomography (CT)-based fusion assessment at 12 months. The operative strategy emphasized continuous endoscopic visualization of the ENR during corridor creation, foraminoplasty, disc space preparation, and cage insertion.

Results

Diagnoses included isthmic spondylolisthesis in 11 patients and foraminal stenosis in 9 patients. The mean preoperative disc height at the safety triangle was 2.6 ± 1.3 mm. At 12 months, segmental lordotic angle increased from 12.4° ± 6.6° to 14.6° ± 5.8° (P = 0.0046), and slip distance decreased from 5.5 ± 2.8 mm to 3.1 ± 2.9 mm (P = 0.001). Oswestry Disability Index improved from 32.5 ± 11.2 to 15.7 ± 12.8 (P < 0.0001). Numerical rating scale scores improved from 5.8 ± 1.6 to 2.8 ± 2.3 for low back pain (P < 0.0001) and from 3.8 ± 2.7 to 2.0 ± 2.2 for leg pain (P = 0.0014). The preliminary CT-based fusion rate at 12 months was 88.0%. No ENR injury, infection, or reoperation occurred.

Conclusions

A structured, level-specific strategy for UBE trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion was feasible at L5/S1 and was associated with significant clinical improvement, modest radiological correction, and an 88.0% preliminary CT-based fusion rate at 12 months. Further studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to validate these findings.

Clinical relevance

This study provides a level-specific framework for performing UBE trans-Kambin lumbar interbody fusion at L5/S1, a level with substantial anatomical and technical constraints.

Level of evidence: 4

title: In Vivo Detection of Ampullary T2 Hypointensity as a Marker of Vestibular Atelectasis.
abstract:
Background and purpose

Vestibular atelectasis (VA) is a histologically defined collapse of the membranous labyrinth, often accompanied by dense basophilic deposits. While delayed postcontrast 3D-FLAIR imaging allows indirect visualization of VA, no in vivo correlate of the basophilic deposits has been reported. This study describes a novel T2-weighted hypointense signal within the ampullae and utricle as a potential imaging biomarker of VA and explores its clinical relevance in patients with bilateral vestibular areflexia.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study included 47 patients with bilateral vestibular areflexia, confirmed by video Head Impulse Test and vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials. All underwent 3T MRI with delayed postcontrast 3D-FLAIR and high-resolution T2-weighted sequences. The presence and distribution of ampullary or utricular T2 hypointensities were evaluated and correlated with radiological VA, clinical presentation, and vestibular function.

Results

Among the 47 patients included, VA was identified in 32 (68.1%). A distinct T2 hypointense signal was observed in 25 patients (53.2%), exclusively within the VA group. These hypointensities were significantly more prevalent in the superior and posterior ampullae compared to the lateral (FDR-P<0.001). VA patients were significantly younger, had better hearing thresholds and more severe posterior canal dysfunction; short vertigo episodes were more frequent in this group without reaching statistical significance. In age-adjusted Firth logistic regression, ampullary hypointensity was the only variable independently associated with VA (odds ratio: 124.59, 95% CI: 5.35-2900.22; apparent area under the curve: 0.973, 95% CI: 0.890-0.994), although the estimate was imprecise owing to quasi-complete separation (FDR-P=0.0104).

Conclusion

A T2 hypointense signal within the ampullae and utricle was observed exclusively in patients with radiological vestibular atelectasis in this cohort. Its anatomical distribution is compatible with the basophilic deposits described in histopathological series, although this correspondence remains hypothetical in the absence of tissue analysis. This MRI sign may raise suspicion of VA when delayed postcontrast 3D-FLAIR imaging is unavailable or contraindicated, rather than replace it.

title: Smartwatch-based pelvic tracking system for augmented reality navigation in total hip arthroplasty: a preliminary clinical study.
abstract:
Background

Accurate assessment of pelvic orientation is essential for acetabular cup placement during total hip arthroplasty (THA). Conventional pelvic tracking systems generally rely on dedicated tracking hardware and optical tracking infrastructure. We developed a smartwatch-based pelvic tracking system integrated with an augmented reality (AR) navigation platform and evaluated its preliminary clinical performance.

Methods

This retrospective study included 30 hips of 27 consecutive patients who underwent primary THA using a smartwatch-based pelvic tracking navigation system between May 2025 and April 2026. The system utilizes a commercially available smartwatch fixed to the iliac crest as a pelvic tracking device and communicates orientation information to a smartphone-based AR navigation platform via Bluetooth. Acetabular cup orientation was evaluated using postoperative CT. Absolute radiographic inclination (RI) and anteversion (RA) errors were calculated as absolute differences between the final intraoperative navigation measurements and postoperative CT measurements.

Results

The mean absolute RI error was 2.8° ± 2.1°, and the mean absolute RA error was 3.6° ± 2.2°. Postoperative CT measurements were within 5° of the final intraoperative navigation measurements for RI and RA in 86.7% and 70.0% of hips, respectively. Navigation was successfully completed in all 30 hips, with no conversion to a backup technique. Additional bench testing demonstrated reproducible smartwatch reattachment and reduction of time-dependent relative orientation differences following FPP invocation.

Conclusions

This study demonstrated the feasibility of integrating a commercially available smartwatch into a pelvic tracking system for THA navigation. The smartwatch-based pelvic tracking platform achieved a preliminary range of cup-positioning accuracy without requiring continuous optical visualization of a pelvic reference marker while utilizing a compact and widely available consumer wearable device. This study represents the first step toward wearable-device-based navigation in arthroplasty.
